header:
Date: 2025-09-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Neptune - ML Eng), Tom Li (Neptune - CTO), Marta Gomez (Neptune - Infra)
summary: Optimize product walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8), expected latency/quality tradeoffs, and next steps for a short POC. SE demo'd benchmark results on a representative LLM, discussed integration points (API/Console) and security considerations (KMS/SOC2). Agreed to run customer-specific benchmarks and share pricing/bench artifacts.
topics: integration via Redwood API and Console guidance
security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, VPC considerations
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna run through Optimize quantization profiles — INT8 and FP8 — and show the tradeoffs, hi Tom, hi Aisha.
[00:18] Aisha Rahman: Hey, hi Sofia, yeah excited, we've been hitting cost and latency limits so looking forward.
[00:28] Daniel Kim: Cool, I'll kick off with a quick overview of what our quant profiles mean and then show some numbers. Just a heads up some of the slides auto transcribed weirdly so apologies for typos.
[00:45] Tom Li: Sounds good. Quick ask — we care about 95th percentile tail latency more than average. Also, we have a mix of short prompt generation and long chat sessions.
[01:12] Daniel Kim: Totally. So INT8 is more aggressive quantization, typically gives you 2-3x token throughput uplift on Ampere/Blackwell style GPUs with a small quality delta for many tasks; FP8 is a newer middle ground — better quality than INT8 and still lower latency/cost than FP16 but requires model kernels that support it.
[01:48] Marta Gomez: When you say "kernels" are we locked to a specific infra or does Dedicated/Private support it?
[01:58] Daniel Kim: Good q — we support FP8 kernels on our Dedicated fleet on compatible drivers; for Private deployments we provide a prebuilt runtime and kernel selection logic but you may need specific CUDA/driver versions. Hosted API will auto-route to an FP8-enabled variant when available.
[02:25] Aisha Rahman: Any early numbers you can share? We care about quality delta on our classification prompts.
[02:33] Daniel Kim: Yep. So here's a slide I shared: on our internal eval set (mix of summarization, classification, code) INT8 showed ~5-7% drop in a BLEU/ROUGE-like metric for generative tasks and up to 2-3% drop on classification accuracy in worst cases; FP8 reduced that to ~1-2% on generative and <1% on classification, while latency improvements were roughly 2.8x for INT8 and 1.8x for FP8 versus FP16 baseline.
[03:10] Tom Li: 2.8x on INT8 is great but 5-7% ROUGE drop could be a showstopper for our customer-facing summaries.
[03:22] Daniel Kim: Totally, that's why we recommend the following flow: run a quick POC on your representative prompts, inspect the qualitative outputs and run our automated eval suite; also we have prefix/KV cache improvements that often recover apparent quality regressions for short-turn tasks.
[03:50] Sofia Patel: To add — Optimize in the Console will show you per-prompt quality deltas, and we can hook regression alerts so if a rollout to INT8 crosses your acceptance threshold it can auto-roll back.
[04:08] Aisha Rahman: Nice — how accurate are the per-prompt deltas? We need false positives to be low.
[04:18] Daniel Kim: It's based on a mix of lexical and embedding-similarity metrics; for some tasks it's noisy — we always recommend human-in-the-loop checks for the first milestone.
[04:36] [05:00] Demo start — Daniel shares screen of Optimize Console showing quantization profiles panel.
[05:00] Daniel Kim: Okay screen up, this is the quantization profiles tab, you can see an INT8 profile, an FP8 profile, and the FP16 baseline. Each profile has an expected latency multiplier and a quality risk score.
[05:28] Aisha Rahman: I see "quality risk" — how's that computed?
[05:33] Daniel Kim: It's a weighted score from our eval sets; it factors in delta on core metrics and a rollback risk. It's heuristic but helpful for quick triage.
[05:52] Tom Li: Can we set different profiles by route? e.g., summaries go FP16 for high quality, chat short-turn go INT8.
[06:02] Daniel Kim: Absolutely, per-route profile routing is supported; in API you can set profile hints or pin a model variant, in Dedicated you can set per-service routing policies.
[06:18] Aisha Rahman: Any gotchas on embedding quality with INT8? We're using embeddings for search and similarity.
[06:27] Daniel Kim: Good point — embeddings are more sensitive. INT8 tends to degrade nearest-neighbor recall noticeably; FP8 often preserves recall much better. For embeddings we usually recommend FP8 or keep embeddings on FP16 and quantize generation only.
[06:45] Marta Gomez: Architecturally, if we go Dedicated, does Redwood handle driver upgrades for FP8 kernels?
[06:52] Sofia Patel: For Dedicated we manage the runtime and driver in the managed zone; for Private you can opt for Redwood-managed updates or self-managed depending on your compliance needs.
[07:12] [07:30] Daniel runs live benchmark chart: latency (ms) vs tokens/sec for FP16/FP8/INT8 across sequence lengths 32/128/512.
[07:30] Daniel Kim: Here are some numbers — seq32: FP16 50ms, FP8 30ms, INT8 18ms; seq128: FP16 180ms, FP8 120ms, INT8 75ms; seq512 shows smaller relative gains due to KV cache and memory bandwidth.
[08:05] Aisha Rahman: Those seq128 numbers look promising. What about memory footprint — does INT8 let us serve larger context?
[08:15] Daniel Kim: Yes INT8 reduces memory usage enabling larger batch sizes or longer context for the same GPU, but you do need to watch quantization-induced noise in attention.
[08:30] Tom Li: How reproducible are these numbers on our on-prem Ampere boxes versus cloud?
[08:38] Daniel Kim: Should be similar if drivers and kernel libs match; a lot depends on cuBLAS/cuDNN/driver versions. We'll capture exact driver/kernel revisions in the benchmark artifact we send.
[08:55] Aisha Rahman: Can you talk about fallback behavior — say we route to INT8 and hit a spike, do we fallback to FP16?
[09:05] Daniel Kim: Yes — smart routing supports fallback to FP8/FP16 or even to another region. You can configure cost vs latency tiers, and automatic fallback is part of our resilience model.
[09:28] Marta Gomez: On security: KMS for keys, audit logs — anything special for Dedicated/Private?
[09:36] Sofia Patel: We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated; audit logs are available and we can enable extended retention as an add-on. We'll include SOC2/STIG docs in the pack.
[09:50] Tom Li: Great. Back to quality — do you have examples where INT8 is actually fine?
[09:58] Daniel Kim: Yeah for many classification and short response tasks INT8 yields near-identical outputs, and we sometimes see negligible deltas on code generation for small snippets. The bigger gaps appear in abstractive summarization and long-form creative generation.
[10:20] [10:45] Demo — Daniel toggles rollout to show Canary: INT8 canary on 5% traffic with auto-regression detection.
[10:45] Daniel Kim: Canary rollout — here you see the per-prompt diff heatmap and automatic rollback if the weighted quality score exceeds your threshold.
[11:12] Aisha Rahman: How does the per-prompt diff display scale? We have thousands of unique prompts.
[11:20] Daniel Kim: It aggregates by prompt clusters, and you can drill into exemplars; the Console integrates with our eval harness to surface statistically significant regressions.
[11:36] Tom Li: Can we tie this to our internal SLOs and create alerts?
[11:41] Sofia Patel: Yes you can map Redwood metrics to your SLOs via webhooks or integrate with Datadog/Prometheus.
[11:55] Aisha Rahman: About POC length — how long do you usually run the POC to be confident?
[12:02] Daniel Kim: For quantization POCs we suggest 2 weeks of traffic with a focus on representative prompts and edge cases; shorter if you can do synthetic stress tests and heavy sampling.
[12:18] Tom Li: Ok. Cost-wise what are we looking at?
[12:22] Sofia Patel: INT8 typically lowers token cost significantly — we'll share modeled cost savings in the pricing sheet; there are also engineering tradeoffs for Private.
[12:33] [13:00] Question from Marta: Any licensing limits with model weights when doing quantization?
[13:07] Daniel Kim: Model license depends on the model — some open models permit quantization, others have restrictions; we'll map this in the model catalog entry we share.
[13:22] Aisha Rahman: For embeddings again — if FP8 is close in cost to INT8 but much better in recall, seems like a no-brainer.
[13:30] Daniel Kim: Agreed, many customers choose a hybrid: embeddings and critical routes on FP8/FP16, everything else can be INT8.
[13:44] [14:05] Sofia: quick clarification — are you planning Private deployment or Dedicated?
[14:10] Tom Li: Possibly Dedicated to start; Private is on the roadmap if compliance requires it.
[14:20] Daniel Kim: For Dedicated we can schedule a capacity commit estimate after the POC if the numbers look good.
[14:33] Aisha Rahman: Will you be able to run the benchmark on our sample payload? We have some pii but we can obfuscate.
[14:40] Daniel Kim: Yes, we can run on obfuscated samples; for Private we can run in your environment.
[15:00] [15:30] Demo — Daniel opens benchmark artifact spreadsheet: shows per-metric deltas and example outputs.
[15:30] Daniel Kim: I'm showing sample outputs — on one summarization prompt INT8 omitted a key clause, FP8 kept it. The heatmap flags that as high risk.
[16:05] Aisha Rahman: That's exactly the type of thing we care about. Can we configure which metrics matter most?
[16:12] Daniel Kim: Yes you can weight metrics in Optimize so the quality risk score aligns to your business criteria.
[16:30] Tom Li: Any examples of customers that moved to INT8 at scale?
[16:36] Sofia Patel: We have finance and internal search customers that moved non-critical routes to INT8 and saved 30-40% on token cost. We'll anonymize and share a case study.
[16:52] Aisha Rahman: About observability — can we get token-level breakdowns and per-route cost?
[16:58] Daniel Kim: Yup, Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model and you can export to CSV.
[17:12] [18:00] Slight audio glitch, some words dropped — transcription may be off around 18:00-19:00.
[18:10] Tom Li: One final technical — for sequence lengths >1024 do you recommend INT8?
[18:20] Daniel Kim: For very long sequences, INT8 gains diminish because memory bandwidth and KV cache interplay; FP8 or FP16 might be preferable depending on quality.
[18:34] Aisha Rahman: What about reranking pipelines — embeddings are critical there.
[18:40] Daniel Kim: For rerankers we strongly advise FP8 or FP16 for embedding generation.
[18:52] Tom Li: Ok that's helpful.
[19:00] [32:00] Mid-call recap: agreed POC, bench run, pricing sheet, security docs.
[32:10] Sofia Patel: I'll collate the next steps and send a calendar invite for POC planning.
[32:24] Aisha Rahman: Thanks, would appreciate the drill-down on kernel/driver versions for our infra team.
[32:30] Daniel Kim: We'll include exactly which driver versions, kernel builds and runtime flags we used in the bench.
[32:45] Marta Gomez: Also include guidance for autoscaling policies to change between FP8/INT8 — we need to avoid noisy autoscale thrash.
[32:55] Daniel Kim: Good note — we'll include recommended autoscaler thresholds and a sample config.
[33:10] [45:00] Quick questions section — customer asks about audit retention.
[45:08] Sofia Patel: We can extend audit log retention as an add-on; we'll put retention tiers in the security pack.
[45:25] Tom Li: Anything else on pricing for Dedicated?
[45:32] Sofia Patel: We'll provide a Recommended Commit and cost modeling after the POC.
[45:45] Aisha Rahman: One more on model drift detection with quantization changes.
[45:52] Daniel Kim: Optimize supports drift detectors tied to your eval prompts; if drift crosses a threshold it'll flag and you can auto rollback.
[46:10] [56:00] Final recap and close
[56:10] Sofia Patel: Great, to recap: Daniel will run bench and share results, I'll send pricing and security docs, Aisha will share sample prompts; we'll meet week of 9/22 to plan the POC.
[56:30] Tom Li: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[56:38] Aisha Rahman: Thanks all.
[56:45] Sofia Patel: Thanks, bye.
[57:00] Meeting ended.
